items.settingsPath: Turn Windows features on or off, and tick SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support. Note that SMB 1 is insecure and Microsoft removed it for a reason.
items.name: Remove SMB 1.0
items.desc: The 1980s file sharing protocol, still shipped as an optional feature. Windows 11 does not install it by default, so on most machines this finds nothing and says so.
items.riskNote: You lose access to file shares that only speak SMB1: Windows XP machines, and some NAS boxes and printers that were never updated. Everything from Vista onward speaks SMB2 or later.

items.settingsPath: Control Panel > System > Remote settings, and allow Remote Assistance connections.
items.name: Turn off Remote Assistance
items.desc: Stops anyone connecting to this machine through the Windows Remote Assistance invitation path. Remote Desktop is a separate feature and is not affected.

items.name: Turn off LLMNR name resolution
items.desc: Windows falls back to shouting a name across the local network when DNS has no answer. That broadcast is trivially answered by anyone else on the network, which is how credential relay attacks start.
items.riskNote: Devices with no DNS entry - some printers, some NAS boxes, other PCs on a router that does not register names - may stop being reachable by name. Reaching them by IP address still works, and mDNS handles most modern devices.

items.name: Prefer IPv4 and turn off IPv6 tunnels
items.desc: Leaves IPv6 itself working on real network adapters, but stops the Teredo, 6to4, and ISATAP tunnel interfaces and puts IPv4 first when a site answers on both. Takes effect after a restart.
items.riskNote: Teredo is what some peer-to-peer features use to reach each other through a router, Xbox multiplayer among them. If party chat or matchmaking breaks after this, that is why.
